advisories.title: D-128 and the adopted D-126 record two different artifacts against DR-105 under a byte-identical descriptor — 'DR-105 leftover T2-02 successor candidate' — and the draft distinguishes the two strands only by implication
advisories.location: Draft title (line 1) and Decision item 1 (lines 57-59), against COORD line 5197
advisories.observation: COORD line 5197 is 'D-126 — Record host-effect-authorization.v25 as DR-105 leftover T2-02 successor candidate', ADOPTED 2026-08-15, and its Decision line reads 'Record v25 as DR-105's leftover T2-02 successor candidate'. This draft's title and Decision item 1 use that descriptor verbatim for a different artifact, permission-truth-tables.v9, on the same register row, in the same calendar day. After adoption COORD will carry two adjacent decisions whose recording labels are indistinguishable, and the draft never states in one place that these are two distinct strands of DR-105's leftover. The distinction is real and I verified it: file 08 line 287 carries both lineages separately, naming the host-effect candidate recorded at D-093 and, separately, 'permission-truth-tables.v2 remains the accepted DR-105 design-contract candidate (D-042)'. D-032 is what splits them — the row records that 'host-under-instruction is outside this vocabulary'. So the permission-truth-tables lineage (v2 at D-042, v6 at D-109, now v9) and the host-effect lineage (v8 at D-093, v25 at D-126) are genuinely parallel, not competing.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The draft does disclaim the collision, just not in one place. Line 22 states 'It does not retarget D-093, D-126, or D-127'; item 5 states 'Does not record FC-C1, apply host-effect'; item 7 lists D-093 and D-126 among decisions not overturned; and item 3 pins the permission-truth-tables lineage explicitly by naming v6 as the D-109 subject and v2 as the D-042 subject at their reproduced digests. Read with its own disclaimers the record is not ambiguous. Decisively, both candidates bind NOTHING and leave DR-105 OPEN, so even a reader who misread D-128 as displacing D-126 would derive no authority from the error — there is no grant on either side to transfer. That bounds the defect to legibility, which is honesty work, not a condition of adoption.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional and not a condition of adoption. A future recording on a row that already carries a candidate under the same descriptor could name the strand in the label — for example 'permission-vocabulary strand' versus 'host-effect strand' — or add one clause stating that both candidates stand in parallel under D-032.

advisories.title: The 'Does not SATISFY' enumeration in Decision item 7 carries forward, byte-identically, the same internal asymmetry recorded at D-125, D-126 and D-127
advisories.observation: Measured against file 08 lines 283-312, the thirty slice-affecting V2 rows are DR-101 through DR-130 and comprise 4 SATISFIED (DR-102, DR-115, DR-119, DR-123), 2 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED (DR-104, DR-118), 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW (DR-107, DR-122) and 22 OPEN — arithmetic I rebuilt row by row and which reproduces file 08's own condition-2 cell at line 403 exactly. The draft names 23 rows and produces three asymmetries. DR-115 is named although already SATISFIED, while DR-102, DR-119 and DR-123, also SATISFIED, are omitted. DR-107 is omitted although PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, while DR-122 with the identical status is named. DR-128, DR-129 and DR-130 are omitted although all three are OPEN. Diffing this draft against the adopted D-127 draft shows the enumeration is unchanged to the byte, and it is byte-identical to the enumeration in the ADOPTED D-126 record at COORD lines 5240-5245; only the surrounding 'Does not overturn' list grew, correctly, by D-042, D-126 and D-127.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The enumeration is not the operative scope bound. 'Readiness effect: Zero. Condition 2 stays 4 of 30 SATISFIED' binds all thirty rows at once, and I verified that arithmetic independently against file 08 rather than accepting it. Critically, the subject row of this decision — DR-105 — is expressly named in the list and independently confirmed OPEN at file 08 line 287, where the row's own text ends 'This row is not SATISFIED'. So the one row this decision actually touches is disclaimed. The omission of DR-128 is worth a second look given this decision is numbered D-128, but it is not a case of the draft quietly exempting its own namesake: DR-128 is omitted in the adopted D-125, D-126 and D-127 records too, and the draft separately and explicitly addresses it at lines 15-17. Charging it here would contradict the precedent this draft correctly follows, and I graded it advisory on the same reasoning in the preceding cycle.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional and not a condition of adoption. A future recording could enumerate every non-SATISFIED row, or state the bound solely by the condition-2 count and drop the enumeration.

advisories.title: The measured-inputs table pins no digest for v8, the generation v9 actually succeeds and whose two SHOULD-FIX findings it repairs, although both v9 reviewers pinned it explicitly
advisories.location: Measured-inputs table (draft lines 31-39) against Decision item 1's 'successor candidate' characterisation
advisories.observation: The draft records v9 as a 'successor candidate' and its table pins v6 and v2. Neither is what v9 succeeds. v9's own /basedOn declares predecessor docs/coop/artifacts/permission-truth-tables.v8.json at 6b45f642f682e5111dd9347c4bc9405510bae58a810fcd3dc3b2509f709d71fc, with method 'v9 is v8 with targeted repair of CLAUDE-V8-S1 and PTT8-CX-01'. Both frozen v9 verdicts pin v8 independently — the Claude 2 verdict measures it live in measurementsPassed[1], and the Codex verdict carries inputCustody.predecessorV8Sha256 at the same value with allReproduced=true. The recording that rests on those two verdicts is therefore one pin thinner on the succession claim than either reviewer was.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The omission is correctly scoped rather than careless, and I checked this rather than assuming it. Grepping COORD for the lineage returns only permission-truth-tables.v2 (6 occurrences) and v6 (4 occurrences); v7 and v8 were never recorded by any coordinator decision. The table's purpose in this draft is retarget discipline — it pins the two generations that ARE recorded subjects, v2 at D-042 and v6 at D-109, so that item 3's 'those subjects remain' claim is verifiable. v8 is not a recorded subject, so no retarget risk attaches to it. And v8 is not unpinned in substance: it is pinned inside v9's own /basedOn, and v9 itself is pinned in the table at 05d55964, so the succession chain is transitively fixed to the byte by a digest the draft does carry. A claim verifiable from a pinned digest is not an unpinned claim.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. A future recording of a successor candidate could carry the immediate predecessor's digest as a table row alongside the recorded-subject pins, matching what both independent verdicts already do.
